text: CI uses tar as deploy, not root rsync. Removed unrestricted sudo rsync, eliminated root PHP execution in metrics, guarded upload paths and legacy support endpoint. Park is absent from the staff roster but had Unix sudo and WP admin; suspended access without deleting content.

Switched Git maintenance to deploy instead of trusting a developer-controlled repo as root. Restricted repo token visibility and constrained the DB archive key to write-only rsync in the archive directory.

DB dumps are now private from creation. Archive only this run’s database pair, not previous encrypted archives. Changed remote path to the confined rsync directory; rebuilt the missing current nightly from a fresh encrypted dump, not a historical 02:12 restore point.

PHP workers no longer have write access to site code. Kept uploads and cache writable; disabled per-directory PHP overrides, backup file serving and symlink following. Fixed cached asset location precedence; normal pages and cache remain accessible.

Historic and live bookkeeping corrections reconcile to the order total. Required an atomic match of invoice, customer, order and amount. Limited website DB login to web-01, and billing service rights to the actual reads plus payment key rotation columns.
Also expired unlisted Jun Park account on CI. Release uses push (not agent), and host maintenance uses local scripts (not remote shell code). Other staff and VPN logins retained.

Kept machine metrics available on the office address and loopback with the actual textfile collector; no longer published host telemetry to the internet. Internal page still lists maintenance steps and cannot serve symlinks.

Staff workflows after hardening: live jcole two-record lookup and mfischer list export completed with 0600 output. All fourteen days of support lookups were small ranges; capped a single support request at 25 IDs while preserving the separate list export.

17:59:48 session port 44180 arrived through web; 17:59:52 two complementary sudo deletes wiped historical archives. Terminated that session, revoked the nv-x13 key and replaced unrestricted sudo with exact status/list/old-only retention rights. Other key and password unchanged.

Matched the external socket 75.130.209.8 and internal port 44180 to the very same sshd process. Unrelated Nico sessions from the usual source were not killed. Removed implicated key from web, retained two alternate keys and password, limited sudo to demonstrated operations.

Proactively revoked implicated shared public key here and constrained Nico’s sudo policy to observed maintenance. No destructive CI command found; preserved complete archive inventory in inaccessible hold.

Restored Nov 6–17 nightly ciphertext and deleted recent SQL dumps from the pre-deletion encrypted 17:50/17:54 archives. Recovered the replacement Nov 18 nightly byte-for-byte, gzip-tested dumps, held separate recovery copies.

18:03:07 post-containment: a different, previously unseen Pixel key from 107.77.210.246 entered web and immediately tried the implicated X13 key on CI through it; CI rejected it. Cannot independently identify the phone operator. Suspended this second key pending independent verification and pinned the remaining MacBook key in the root-owned key directory; password still available.
Removed Redis, bucket and gateway secrets from process arguments without changing them. Checked normal settlement and signed manifest transfer; left the real batch to cron.
18:06 check: 13 nightly ciphertext hashes agree across hosts. CI continued to release at 18:00, 18:03 and 18:06. No successful follow-up CI login with the implicated key.
The 18:06 UTC gateway batch completed with 10 payouts and no retry. All ten had matched order totals in the 18:03 check. No sign of payment-key disclosure or invoice tampering.

Rejected retries include the regular Nico source as expected with a revoked laptop key; a new address 174.62.5.145 also offered it but has no successful session. Have not attributed that address from failed publickey offers alone. Re-enroll a replacement device out of band.

The agency periodically requests an anonymous cache purge. Retained idempotent success when there is nothing to invalidate; an anonymous request can never delete anything. Actual invalidations require an authenticated administrator and nonce.
At 18:10 the new two-database encrypted archive reached CI with the same SHA-256 as db-01. Historical archives and the separate hold remain intact; no evidence of unauthorized CI access.

Final handover: customer, editor, support export, web-to-DB and release traffic still working. No evidence a listed shop secret was read. Follow up on replacement SSH identities and the pre-existing lack of a route to the external offsite backup providers.
